Chapter Six: The Simplicity and Strangeness of Jesus’ Commands.
Sometimes, it’s the instructions that sound the easiest that actually challenge us the most. Think about these: “Love your enemies.” “Turn the other cheek.” Or, “Give to those who ask.”
These words were spoken so long ago, but if you’re anything like me, they still echo in your mind—especially when life gets tough. At first, they almost sound naïve, don’t they? A bit too idealistic for a world where you’re told to look out for yourself, to be clever and protective.
Picture this: You’ve been wronged by a neighbor. Maybe they said something hurtful, or acted unfairly. The anger simmers, and you can almost feel that urge to get even. Friends might tell you, “Hey, stand up for yourself. Don’t let them walk all over you.” But then, those strange words from Jesus come back—a quiet invitation to respond with kindness instead of payback.
Honestly, that choice can feel pretty unnatural. Maybe even foolish. Still, there’s something deep inside that whispers, this is how things are supposed to be.
Most of us don’t really see how radical these commands are until we actually try to follow them. The world expects us to hit back, not to forgive. It’s one thing to talk about love in theory—but showing love to someone who’s hurt you? That’s a whole different challenge.
The first time you try, it might feel awkward. Maybe even forced. But with every little step—a gentle word, deciding not to escalate, maybe just a quiet prayer for the person who wronged you—your heart starts to shift.
And you start to see: these commands aren’t about being weak or letting people walk over you. They’re about a different kind of strength—the kind that won’t let bitterness or fear decide who you become. It’s an invitation to live in a new way, trusting that love actually has the power to break old patterns of hurt.
Over time, what once felt strange somehow starts to feel freeing. The weight of resentment lifts, and suddenly, there’s space for peace to grow.
Let’s be honest. In a world that celebrates clever moves and self-defense, the simplicity of Jesus’ commands really does stand out. They’re not easy—but they are possible. And if you’re willing to give them a real try, you might just find yourself stepping into a life full of unexpected, life-changing grace.
